raw_source_facts.fact: O is full real O(n) with Haar probability; each determinant component has mass 1/2; mu_(n,b) is the conditioned probability measure; U=O_11. SO(n) alone cannot supply the signed H or factor2.

A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T); p_O denotes the actual density of N(0,A_O^-1). p4 expands its normalization as (2*pi)^(-n/2)*sqrt(det A_O) times the precision quadratic exponential. The seal literal p uses Euclidean volume and this precision convention, not covariance A_O.

For lambda>=0, h_lambda=exp(-lambda*norm(x)^2), H=E_Haar[det(O)*integral_Rn h_lambda(x)p_O(x)dx]. H=(E_(P_+)h_lambda-E_(P_-)h_lambda)/2; hence the actual ordered mixture gap is 2H, not H. The sealed v is H.

Conjugation invariance and covariance of precision/density radialize the averaged signed density. I<=A_O<=kappa I and |det O|=1 give a joint integrable radial Gaussian dominator for lambda>=0, enabling Fubini and Gaussian integration. a=kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U>=2+4lambda>0 on |U|<=1. Eq15 requires h Borel and E|h(U)| finite, which must be derived internally for h(u)=a(u)^(-n/2).

H(lambda)=((-1)^(n-1)*(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^(n/2))*E[((sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1))/(kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U)^(n/2)]. Oe1 is uniform on the Euclidean unit sphere, so its first coordinate U uses normalized surface probability. This law transfer is a dependency, not a caller-supplied law.

r=(1-1/n)*(s-1)/(s+1), s=sqrt(kappa), and lambda=(kappa-1)*(1+r^2)/(8r)-(kappa+1)/4=(4*n*s+(s-1)^2)/(8*n*(n-1)). Under n>=3,kappa>=4 the source asserts 0<r<1 and lambda>0. lambda=0 gives the undecreased r=(s-1)/(s+1) and H(0)=0; the selected theorem is the decreased-r, positive-lambda case.

For every relevant U, kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U=((kappa-1)/(2r))*(1+r^2-2rU)=(n*(s+1)^2/(2*(n-1)))*(1+r^2-2rU). Both scale and sphere denominator are positive. Power splitting at real exponent n/2 requires those domains.

The two Poisson moments of normalized uniform sphere coordinate give E[(1+r^2-2rU)^(-n/2)]=1/(1-r^2) AND E[U*(1+r^2-2rU)^(-n/2)]=r/(1-r^2), with 0<r<1. Linear combination gives the selected numerator =-(s-1)/(n*(1-r^2)). The sealed promoted identity is exactly this latter source use-site on the literal normalized volume.toSphere measure.

Eq21 AND selected Eq22/23 scaling AND the selected numerator yield H(lambda)=((-1)^n/n)*((s-1)/(s+1))^n*(1-1/n)^(n/2)/(1-r^2). The sign and integer n-powers must remain distinct from real half-dimension powers. The source-derived value alone is insufficient to establish the sealed L1 conjunction without the internal regularity/law-density bridge.
